audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3..5].side read 'Skill' and phases[6].side read 'Kassadin' while content win[] read Brand on all seven rows and the packet chart is Brand x7. phases[6] also argued with itself: side Kassadin under a why describing Brand detonating the teamfight.
audit.why: Two of three sources (packet levelChart and content win[]) say Brand every row, and the 59.27% win rate over 248 games agrees. Kassadin's late-game case is real but nothing on this page supports flipping only the last row while its own sentence says the opposite.
audit.corrected: phases[3..6].side = Brand, matching win[] and the packet; whys already describe Brand owning those stages so they stand unchanged.

audit.why: Brand: level 3 E-Q package, level 6 Pyroclasm (100s rank 1), Liandry's. Kassadin: level 6 Riftwalk and then two items — his spike is item-gated, not level-gated, and Void Stone's magic reduction compounds with every MR item.
audit.corrected: enemyWin rewritten to name the actual spike instead of 'landing Riftwalk'.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text claimed Null Sphere has no shield — Riot's text says it grants a shield that absorbs magic damage. Several fields treated Riftwalk as a cooldown you can wait out; it is 5/3.5/2s for 40 mana. Void Stone's flat magic damage reduction, which applies to every spell Brand owns, was never stated. Nether Blade's auto-attack reset was never used as a burst tell.
audit.why: All four are directly in the kit files. Brand's entire kit is magic damage, so Void Stone plus a Null Sphere shield is the decisive interaction of this matchup.
audit.corrected: Fixed the shield claim, replaced 'wait for Riftwalk' advice with mana-gating, and put the Nether Blade reset in wants.foe as the melee tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns had no digit, and pointed at Riftwalk — the one cooldown that is never meaningfully down.
audit.why: Force Pulse at 21s rank 1 is the punishable cooldown; Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Rewrote around Force Pulse and Sear's 8s.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.foe[2] said Kassadin silences you; no silence appears in Riot's text for any of his abilities in this kit file.
audit.why: Null Sphere's text says it interrupts channels — it says nothing about silencing, and Brand has no channel for it to interrupt.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the verified Nether Blade auto-reset opener.

edits.before: - Kassadin Riftwalk: matchup-defining — His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Count it out loud if you must. - Your E-Q stun package has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 and 2s maxed, so it is never truly down — gate him on mana instead. - Force Pulse is 21s at rank 1: the moment he spends it you own twenty seconds of walk-up. - Your Sear is 8s early, so poke before he charges it again.

edits.before: Carry through AoE math — no burst mage damages three targets like Brand; your job is the spacing that lets the bounces vote.
edits.after: Carry by denying the scaling: shove, hover his jungle, and make Kassadin farm at 400 range under tower instead of stacking items.

edits.before: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. Until it’s spent, every commit is a coin flip.
edits.after: Riftwalk closes 500 units for 40 mana — hold the ablaze-then-stun package to answer the blink, not to poke with.

edits.before: E the instant ablaze, Q the stun, W the stunned body, walk — the full package chunks half a bar and the burn writes the receipt.
edits.after: Riftwalk only travels 500 units, so a wave held mid-lane forces him to blink twice to reach you and you see the first one.

edits.before: Kassadin burns Riftwalk on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Pyroclasm bounces stack Blaze to max on champions, arming your Sear stun.

edits.before: That is Kassadin’s whole plan in one window — decline politely and watch it retire.
edits.after: Conflagration is 13s at rank 1 — with it down you have no ablaze, so no stun.

edits.before: Your stun only exists on ablaze targets — a Q thrown at a clean health bar is the most expensive miss in your kit.
edits.after: Riftwalk turns any deep wave into a free flank, and Void Stone already trims every point of magic damage you land.

edits.before: W-poking on cooldown with Q unbanked while his engage is loaded — Brand without the stun threat is a bonfire waiting for company.
edits.after: A third Pillar of Flame costs 100 mana at rank 5 and leaves you standing still inside the 500 units Riftwalk needs to reach you.

edits.before: Stun-burn the dive, tax the roams with shove, and out-scale his patience. Shorthand: Riftwalk down, wave right, go.
edits.after: Stun-burn him off the wave pre-6 and tax his mana. Riftwalk is 5s at rank 1 — punish his position, never wait for it to be down.

edits.before: Track Kassadin’s Riftwalk: His mobility spike — the lane is decided before it scales. It’s down or you don’t go.
edits.after: Track Kassadin's mana, not Riftwalk: at 5s and 40 mana it is always up, so his bar is the only real gate.

edits.before: Kassadin is scaling-locked early — his Null Sphere has no shield to protect him from your Q-W combo, and his mana pool is so bad he can barely trade back before running dry.
edits.after: Kassadin is scaling-locked early — Null Sphere's magic shield only comes around every 9s at rank 1, and his mana pool is so thin he can barely trade back before running dry.

edits.before: Silence you to stop your combo in forced fights
edits.after: Open with a Nether Blade auto-attack reset in melee

notes: The channel-interruptible missing-interaction is a flag misfire: Riot's text says Null Sphere INTERRUPTS channels, it is not itself a channel, and Brand has no channelled ability — nothing to write. The autoreset one is real and went into wants.foe[2], which previously claimed a silence that appears nowhere in Kassadin's kit text. Full-layer phases[3..6].side disagreed with content win[] (Skill/Skill/Skill/Kassadin vs Brand x4); aligned to win[] and the packet chart, which also removes phases[6] arguing against its own why. Paired win[N] edits included as unchanged pairs to keep the chart group atomic. Void Stone's flat magic damage reduction applies to Brand's entire kit and deserves more page space than one clause — flagged for a later pass rather than expanded here inside the length band.
